turns.answer_text:
The 300 heats split into three process families, and they are not close:

- **Carburized / case-hardened** (32 heats: CT=930, THT=30, Tt=120, TT=160–200) → **838–1190 MPa** (mean ~1010)
- Through-hardened (260 heats) → 325–906 MPa (mean ~506)
- Normalized only (8 heats) → ~225–275 MPa

So the high-strength **plateau** is the carburizing route, not a one-off spike. Every carburized heat stays strong; a ±5% nudge cannot jump CT/THT/Tt across the huge gaps that separate families (e.g. CT 930→883.5 is still carburizing; THT 30→31.5 is still “no through-harden”).

Within that plateau two alloy clusters sit at the top:

| Cluster | n | targets | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ni–Cr–Mo (C=0.23, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Mo=0.18) | 2 | **1124, 1190** | highest ceiling |
| Cr–Mo (C=0.21, Cr=1.17, Mo=0.17) | 4 | 1074–1144 | most replicated |

I take the **Ni–Cr–Mo** chemistry (best heats) but the **interior process** of the 1124 heat, not the 1190 record:

- 1190 uses Ct=540 + QmT=140 — a unique combo. A sister Ni-steel with that same process is only 935 MPa, so that corner is sharp.
- 1124 uses Ct≈470 + QmT=60. Nearby Ni-steels at that setting are 1034–1124, a broad shelf.
- TT=160 (27/32 carburized heats) not 200; low temper keeps case hardness, and +5% (168) stays below the ~180 model split.
- DT=850 / Dt=15 is the pairing actually used with this alloy (the Cr-cluster’s 896/70.2 is a different recipe).
- Low P (0.008), Mo≈0.18, RedRatio=860 (the high end of the carburized range; within-family corr +0.57).
- Inclusions left at the observed values of this cluster (dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0); trees split on dA, so dropping it is a fake “optimum”.

Ensemble check (RF/GB/ET/Ridge/Huber/SVR/KNN): **~1119 MPa**. Nearest real heat is the 1124 MPa Ni-steel (scaled distance 0.08). Under ±5% in any one variable the only material moves are NT 930→883.5 (~−40, still ~1080) and Tt 120→114 (~−18). Everything else moves by a few MPa. That is a shelf, not a peak.

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=480, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=60, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0

        rf.predict(x)[0],
        gb.predict(x)[0],
        et.predict(x)[0],
        hgb.predict(x)[0],
        ridge.predict(x)[0],
    ])
    return preds

def robustness(xdict):
    x0 = np.array([xdict[f] for f in features], dtype=float)
    p0 = predict_ens(x0)
    worst_delta = 0
    worst_var = None
